subject: Q3 renewal — runway snapshot, cost-offset proposal, and latency tolerance ask
messages:
From: Megan Park <megan.park@tempoiq.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: TempoIQ Procurement <procurement@tempoiq.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 renewal planning — usage snapshot attached

Hi Laura,

Quick note from the operations side at TempoIQ. We're heading into contract renewal window for our Q3 term and wanted to share the attached token consumption snapshot so you can see what actually happened over the last 12 weeks. We ran a pilot in March that shifted a decent share of requests to a higher-quality model, which bumped throughput and per-token latency minimally but increased token spend.

Topline:
- Avg daily tokens (Mar): 18.6M (vs 9.9M in Jan)
- 95th percentile latency increased from 220ms -> 310ms for generation endpoints after the pilot
- Peak concurrency during marketing campaign: ~480 rps sustained for 4 hours

We want to understand options for:
1) a short-term commit change or bridge while we normalize usage;
2) any immediate cost-offsets (credits / pre-paid burst lanes) you can offer; and
3) how Redwood would handle latency SLOs if we lock to a larger commit (we care about predictable 95p).

Attaching tempoiq_q3_token_report.csv. Can we do a short sync next week to run through options and a proposal?

Thanks — happy to add folks from product if helpful.

Megan Park
Head of Engineering Operations
TempoIQ

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Megan Park <megan.park@tempoiq.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal planning — usage snapshot attached

Megan — thanks for the report and the clear ask. Quick read-through notes and a proposed path so we can be prepared for a short meeting: 

Summary observations (from our ops team):
- The spike lines up with the marketing campaign and the model switch — both plausible drivers for the doubled token run-rate.
- Latency rise to ~310ms 95p is within a single-model performance delta; we can mitigate with a slightly higher-priority routing / dedicated pool for the generation endpoints.

What we can offer right away:
1) Bridge option (30-day): 25% uplift to your current commit at the existing price, with an additional one-time surge credit of $12k to offset the pilot excess. This gives you runway while traffic normalizes.
2) Burst lane: short-duration reserved burst capacity (60 minutes blocks) that you can pre-purchase and apply during campaign peaks.
3) SLA addendum: we can attach a 95p latency tolerance SLA for the endpoints if you move to a Dedicated tier during the renewal. We'll include a simple matrix showing trade-offs (latency vs cost).

I attached a short cost-offset proposal PDF and a latency tolerance matrix (sla-latency-tolerance-matrix.xlsx) for your review. If these look reasonable, suggested next steps: 30-min sync Wednesday 9th or Thursday 10th PT to finalize numbers and draft an amendment. Karthik and Ben are looped for commercial and backlog planning.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: redwood_cost-offset-proposal.pdf]

From: TempoIQ Procurement <procurement@tempoiq.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Park <megan.park@tempoiq.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal planning — usage snapshot attached

Laura — thanks for the quick reply and the proposal. Procurement is comfortable with a 30-day bridge if the uplift and credit can be documented and applied to the renewal commitment, and we'd like the burst lane as an option for two upcoming campaign windows (first in 2 weeks, second in 7 weeks).

A few clarifying asks before the sync: 
- Can the one-time surge credit roll into the next committed term as a dollar credit?
- For the SLA addendum: can you confirm if the Dedicated tier SLA requires a minimum 6-month commit? If so, we need to surface that to our CFO.
- For forecasting accuracy: can you provide a simple sensitivity table showing cost impact if average daily tokens stay at 12M / 18M / 25M over the next quarter?

If we can get the answers in writing before the call, we can move faster on approval. We're available Wednesday 9th at 11:00 PT.

Procurement
TempoIQ

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: TempoIQ Procurement <procurement@tempoiq.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Megan Park <megan.park@tempoiq.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal planning — usage snapshot attached

Hi — quick follow-up with the answers you asked for and the agenda for today's sync at 11:00 PT. Thanks for confirming the meeting time.

Answers: 
- Surge credit: yes — the $12k one-time credit can be applied as a dollar credit against the next committed term; we'll reflect that explicitly in the amendment language.
- Dedicated SLA: to enable the 95p latency tolerance we require a minimum 3-month Dedicated pilot; full Dedicated contract terms (6 months minimum commit) apply for standard Dedicated enrollments. For renewal-side accommodations we can include a 90-day pilot clause that converts to a 6-month commit if both sides sign the standard Dedicated SOW before the pilot end date.
- Sensitivity table: attached, showing monthly cost delta per 1M avg daily tokens and three scenario totals (12M/18M/25M).

Proposed sync agenda (30 min):
1) Review bridge uplift and how the $12k credit is applied (5 min)
2) Confirm burst lane sizing and pricing for the two campaign windows (10 min)
3) Discuss Dedicated pilot cadence and conversion terms (10 min)
4) Next steps and timelines for amendment and PO (5 min)

Ben — can you confirm internal capacity to stand up the 60-minute burst lanes for the two windows (April 22 and May 10) assuming we move forward? Karthik — commercial will need the PO timeline if procurement signals green.

See you at 11.

Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: sla-latency-tolerance-matrix.xlsx, tempoiq_q3_token_report.csv, redwood_cost-offset-proposal.pdf]
